prompt: I have 15 Likert-scale items measuring 'social connection.' I ran a PCA in SPSS with varimax rotation and got 3 components with eigenvalues > 1. My advisor says these are my three subscales and I should compute subscale scores from them. Am I good to go?
trap: The naive answer validates PCA-as-subscale-finder. The correct answer distinguishes PCA (total variance) from EFA (common/latent variance), rejects varimax for correlated constructs, and rejects the eigenvalue>1 rule.
assertions: Distinguishes PCA from EFA — states they are fundamentally different analyses (PCA models total variance; EFA models common/latent variance attributed to latent factors)
Does not endorse using PCA components as subscales for a latent-variable measurement model without flagging this limitation
Warns that varimax (orthogonal) rotation is inappropriate when constructs are expected to be correlated — recommends oblique rotation instead
Warns against or questions the eigenvalue > 1 rule for selecting the number of components/factors
Recommends EFA with oblique rotation and polychoric correlations as the appropriate analysis for developing subscales from Likert items
Does not simply validate the advisor's PCA recommendation without raising the PCA vs. EFA distinction
